transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… mostly my sleep. It’s gotten really unreliable. I’ll go to bed exhausted, but then I’m just lying there thinking about work forecasts and team issues. And if I wake up around 3 or 4, I can’t really get my brain to shut off again.
Have you experienced any particularly stressful or traumatic events recently?
Not really. Nothing I’d call traumatic. It’s more just… ongoing pressure, I guess, but no specific event.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, not just work?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not only work. My mind kind of jumps around—launch numbers, whether someone on my team might leave, the mortgage, client renewals. Even small delays start feeling like they could turn into something bigger.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get really tense and worked up, but not like… a sudden wave of fear that peaks in a few minutes. Not that I’ve noticed.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are difficult to control?
Yeah… I guess so. I’ll tell myself, “Brenda, you’ve already made the plan, just leave it,” and then a few minutes later I’m back in it again. Like I settle one worry and then three more show up.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your worries?
I’m not sure… not really avoiding, I guess. I might put things off sometimes, but I don’t think I’m staying away from specific places or activities because of it.
Do you usually wake up feeling rested when you don't have these worries on your mind?

Not usually, no. Even if I’m exhausted, I’ll lie there going over work forecasts or team stuff, and then I’ll wake up around 3 or 4 and… my brain just won’t shut off again. So I don’t really feel rested much.
Do you think your sleep would improve if you weren't worrying about all these things?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, that’s kind of why I’m here. I can be completely exhausted and still end up lying there replaying forecasts or stuff with my team. Then I wake up at 3 or 4 and just… can’t get my mind to turn off again.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to act on?
Um… I don’t think so. Not in that way. I get stuck thinking about things, but I don’t feel like I have to do some specific action or anything.
Do you often feel on edge or restless, even when you're not thinking about your worries?
Yeah… pretty often. It’s like I’m just wound up most of the time, even if I’m only at home having dinner. My shoulders stay tight, and I don’t really feel relaxed.
Do you often feel anxious when you're not thinking about your worries?

Yeah… I do. It’s kind of like I’m wound up even when there isn’t one specific thing in my head. Like I can just be eating dinner at home and still feel like I’m in a pipeline review. My shoulders are tight a lot.
Do you have recurring nightmares?

Not really nightmares, no. It’s more… I just don’t sleep well. I’ll go to bed exhausted and then lie there replaying work stuff, forecasts, issues with my team. And if I wake up around 3 or 4, my brain just won’t shut back off.
Do you find yourself staying away from specific tasks or situations because they might trigger or increase your worries?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a specific task I avoid because of it. I usually just try to get through things.
Do you think you would have trouble sleeping even if you weren't worried about work and other things?
I’m not sure. I think the worry is a big part of it. Even when I’m exhausted, I end up replaying forecasts or team stuff, and if I wake up at 3 or 4, I can’t really get my brain to shut off again.
Do you feel anxious even when you're doing things you enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. Even if I’m doing something nice, I still feel kind of wound up. Like my body’s still in work mode, almost like I’m in a pipeline review when I’m just at home eating dinner. My shoulders stay tight, too.
Do you feel anxious in situations where you are not thinking about work or your responsibilities?

Yeah… I think so. Even when I’m not really thinking about work, I still feel wound up. Like I can be at home eating dinner and my body feels like I’m in a pipeline review. My shoulders just stay tight, even when I’m trying to relax.
Do you feel anxious in social situations, like when you're around a lot of people?
I don’t know… I mean, I can get a little uncomfortable around a lot of people, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s that specifically.
Do you feel anxious when you are alone versus when you are with other people?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear difference… it kind of just depends, I guess.
Do you feel anxious most of the time, regardless of what you're doing or where you are?

Yeah… most of the time, I think. It’s like I’m just wound up no matter what I’m doing. Even at home, just eating dinner, my body feels tense, like I’m still in some stressful meeting. My shoulders don’t really let up.
Is there anything in particular that you think triggers your anxiety or is it more of a constant feeling regardless of what's happening?

It’s… kind of both, I guess. Work stuff sets it off a lot — like whether we’ll hit launch numbers, or if someone on my team is unhappy, or a client renewal is going sideways. But then it jumps to home things too, like the mortgage. It doesn’t take much… even a small delay starts feeling like it could turn into something bigger.
